replies.Do you ever get anxious when thinking ab: Not really. My low neuroticism score means I handle stress well. I’ve used math for hobbies like gaming strategies and knitting patterns, so it’s always approachable. Anxiety doesn’t come up because I view it as a tool, not a challenge.
replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: Yes, I used AI tools to check my coding logic and solve math problems. It helped me spot errors quickly and learn new concepts. My experience was positive—AI made complex topics feel manageable without overwhelming me.
replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: First, write the equation in standard form (ax² + bx + c = 0). Then, calculate the discriminant (b² - 4ac). If it’s positive, you get two real roots; if zero, one real root; if negative, complex roots. Finally, plug into the quadratic formula: x = [-b ± √(discriminant)] / (2a).

To find stationary points, take the first derivative f’(x), set it equal to zero, and solve for x. These x-values are where the slope is zero. Plug them back into f(x) to get the y-coordinates. Check if they’re maxima or minima using the second derivative test.
